name: NAIRA MATCHING CENTRE · मॅचिंग सेंटर
one_line: Naira, a couture house from Nashik, runs the festive season as its own Matching Centre: twelve tiles, twelve fabric shades, each with one real piece matched to an outfit, an evening or a person, numbered SHADE N° 01 to N° 12 so the profile becomes the season's shade card.
big_idea: Every Indian town has a matching centre: the shop where a saree goes in and comes out with its blouse piece, fall and petticoat, matched by eye under a tube light. Every woman of 35 to 54 has stood at that counter, and she still matches: jewellery to the Karwa Chauth red, the Paithani to Padwa, five outfits to five wedding functions, a gift to what her mother already wears. Naira really is a couture house (Nashik, made to measure, swatches and tapes on the table), so this season its jewellery counter does the matching. ONE idea a stranger names in three seconds: it's a matching centre; every tile is a fabric shade with a piece matched to it. The grid carries it five ways. (1) THE GRID IS A SHADE CARD: twelve full-bleed fabric shades, each named on its tag SHADE N° 01 to N° 12 in posting order. (2) THE SIGNBOARD: a painted shop board carrying the real NAIRA wordmark opens the run bottom-right (P1, MATCHING CENTRE) and closes it top-left (P12, GUEST ORDERS UNDERTAKEN.), on the grid's long diagonal. (3) THE SHADE TAG: one ivory hang-tag, same size, same corner, same angle on nine covers, tied by a gold thread to the piece; it is this feed's MILNI lockup. (4) FOUR SERIES: THE MATCH (one piece, one evening), SHADE CARD (every colour a piece comes in), माप · THE MEASUREMENTS (exact facts on the tailor's slip and tape), THE SAMPLE BLOUSE (matching for someone who won't say). (5) A WORKING COUNTER: send the outfit on WhatsApp, get three matches back. Execution stays in Naira's shipped register: real product photography and BiRefNet cut-outs only, real Naira Flore couture as swatches, flat colour fields with gold hairlines, Velista caps + Cormorant italic + Jost with one Devanagari line per tile, one piece per frame (sets excepted), no stickers, and a single AI texture in the whole option.
why_it_wins: It finished first of four with the judges (brand & truth 81, reference craft 84, commerce & build 80 = 245/300) and is the only proposal inside all three judges' recommended pairs; every must-fix they raised is applied here. Brand: it is literally true (a couture house matching jewellery the way a matching centre matches a blouse piece) and no demi-fine competitor can borrow it; the couture swatches on P1 slide 2 are the house's own outfits. Reference: it answers the PTAT ask with system rather than costume: a multi-script sign, signboard bookends on the diagonal, one fixed lockup on nine covers, named series with volumes, index carousels, drawn objects (chalni, kandil, blouse flat, tulsi, curtain) framing real pieces, a trial-room reel. Commerce: every post sells a match, a set or a gift in time to arrive (Sample Blouse gift guide 1 Nov; Bhaubeej tile 3 Nov; programme 13 Nov; necklines 15 Nov; ruby set top-left from 22 Nov at ₹5,198 list), ruby leads, the 70-unit necklace and the 79-unit Toggle chain get proof posts, and the BUY2/BUY3 line runs on six captions. Build: 46 frames from a small parametrised kit (tag, pinked swatch, tape, signboard, slip, bill), existing BiRefNet cut-outs plus four new clean mattes already made and registered in cutouts/ (the full Heartbead strand, the Marquise V without its plinth, the closed blush box, the whole Bold Nocturne chain loop), one AI texture, two reels rendered from HTML; the P1 cover was test-rendered from this spec.

system.type_system: Load in every page: kit/tokens.css, kit/scripts.css (P1 slide 4 only needs it), kit/post-base.css. FOUR ROLES, nothing else. (1) HEAD: Velista 400 (kit/fonts/Velista.woff2), uppercase only, letter-spacing .03em, line-height .98, font-variant-ligatures:none (Velista's default liga set turns IS, LIS, ST, TS, TT, NN, UI and V-pairs into swash pairs; 'IS IT GOLD?' rendered with a looped I in testing, so ligatures stay off everywhere). Velista has no ₹, no ·, no °, no en/em dash, no ellipsis: never set a price, a middot, N° or an accented product name (RIVIÈRE, PAVÉ) in Velista; those go in Jost. Words meant to read in the grid are 88px or more. (2) TURN: Cormorant Garamond italic 400, lowercase, 40-56px, line-height 1.12, ends with a full stop. (3) SUPPORT: Jost. Eyebrows and labels Jost 500 caps 18-24px tracking .24-.32em; support copy Jost 400 22-26px tracking .04em; prices always Jost 500 with font-family 'Jost','Poppins' so ₹ falls back to Poppins; the plating kicker '[ 18K GOLD TONE PLATED ]' etc. in Jost 400 18px tracking .24em. Max per slide: one eyebrow + two Jost support lines. (4) SCRIPT: Tiro Devanagari Marathi 400 (kit) for मॅचिंग सेंटर, माप and शुभ दीपावली, 22-64px, ONE Devanagari line per tile (P1 slide 4 is the only exception, using Tiro Devanagari Hindi, Tiro Kannada, Tiro Tamil and Tiro Telugu from kit/scripts.css; all five strings were rendered in Chromium on 25 Oct and shape correctly, but each still needs a named native reader). No Kalam, Rozha, Yatra, Gotu, Playfair or DM Serif anywhere. WORDMARK: kit/naira-wordmark-cream-blush.svg (P1 board, 420px wide = 94px tall) and kit/naira-wordmark-ink-blush.svg (P12 board, 360px wide = 81px tall); never typed, never redrawn, at most once per frame; a photographed or cut-out box lid counts as that frame's wordmark. POSITIONS: 'b300' means the text baseline sits at y=300. Set each line as its own absolutely positioned block, line-height 1, top = b - 0.80 x font-size for Velista and Jost, b - 0.76 x font-size for Cormorant and Tiro, then check the render with body.guides. Punctuation on art: no em dashes, no exclamation marks, no emoji; middot only in Jost lines.

posts.concept: The relaunch after 76 silent days, staged as a shop opening. A painted sage signboard with the real wordmark, NAIRA / MATCHING CENTRE / मॅचिंग सेंटर, hangs over a fan of five pinked fabric swatches; the Ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet lies on the red one, tied to the season's shade tag: SHADE N° 01, MATCHED TO THE RED. The joke is the institution itself: every reader has stood at that counter, and a couture house opening one for its jewellery is both true and funny. The carousel explains the counter the way PTAT's key art explains MILNI: every town has one (with swatches cut from Naira's own couture), how it works, one sign in five scripts, and the four series to come.

posts.why: Karwa Chauth is Thu 29 Oct (Drik Panchang; sources split, so no date on the image) and only 1 of 24 Indian jewellery advertisers mentions it, so the moment is open. The Serpentine Whisper Chain is size-free, gift-friendly, ₹1,299, 20 in stock, and its one cushion stone on a snake chain is the moon on a string, which makes the concept truer. Its proven twin (a solitaire on a chain) is a top-15 seller at Palmonas. posts.concept: The shade card in motion. The cover is a shade-card strip, not a catalogue grid: four tall pinked swatches side by side (ruby, green, organza ivory, amethyst), each holding the same huggie in its stone, under WHICH SHADE ARE YOU? The 12-second loop pushes into each swatch and match-cuts it to the real photograph of that stone, names the shade with its honest correction (green cubic zirconia, not emerald), then lines all four up and asks the viewer to claim one in a word. It turns Edition Two's newest site feature, choosing a stone, into the most commentable question in the feed.

SHOT LIST: 0.00-1.20 s COVER hold, the whole cover layer scales 1.00 to 1.02 linear. 1.20-1.50 s eyebrow, headline and footer fade out (0.3 s). 1.20-1.80 s push into the RUBY swatch: the strip layer scales 1.0 to 1.6 about the ruby swatch's centre (182,1140), ease cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1). 1.50-1.80 s cross-dissolve to the RUBY photo. 1.80 s text 'RUBY.' rises 16px and fades in over 0.5 s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); the italic line follows 0.12 s later. 1.80-3.00 s hold, photo push to 1.03. 3.00 s HARD CUT on the beat to the GREEN flat swatch, 3.35-3.60 dissolve to the emerald-variant photo, text in at 3.60, hold to 4.80. 4.80 s HARD CUT to ivory organza, dissolve 5.15-5.40 to Crystal, text in 5.40, hold to 6.60. 6.60 s HARD CUT to amethyst, dissolve 6.95-7.20, text in 7.20, hold to 8.40. 8.40 s HARD CUT to the END CARD: headline and turn rise in (0.6 s); the four huggies enter left to right from 8.60 s with an 80 ms stagger (opacity 0 to 1, scale .95 to 1, 0.5 s ease-out); labels, price, plating and URL fade in from 9.20 s; hold. 11.40-12.00 s cross-fade 0.6 s back to the COVER composition so frame 360 equals frame 0 (seamless loop). Holds on words are at least 1.2 s; one movement per beat; no shake, spin or whip pans. posts.concept: The wedding card's programme page, read by a matching centre: five functions, five outfits, five matches. The cover is the index (PTAT's [01]-[04] move): HALDI, MEHENDI, SANGEET, PHERAS, RECEPTION, each with one true observation and a small swatch holding its piece, on Paithani purple, the Maharashtrian wedding silk. Inside, one function per slide with the insight that makes the match useful: haldi stains, so wear something small; at mehendi your hands are busy for four hours, so dress your ears; the sangeet needs light from the back row; the pheras are the long one; the reception is the photo line, so its slide is a photograph. The last slide also opens the counter: send us your programme.

To its right, on a small ivory fabric swatch, a pair of gold-tone huggie earrings with green baguette stones, tied to an ivory tag reading Shade N° 11, matched to the guests. posts.why: Tulsi Vivah is Sat 21 Nov (Drik), the traditional opening of the wedding season and the first vivah muhurat. Both the reference and commerce judges flagged a product-free tile in the most-seen row; the guest's green huggies fix that while the plant stays untouched (the brand judge's condition). Green suits the tulsi tile without dressing the plant, and the Emerald variant has 15 in stock. The line is affectionate observation-wit, the kind the owner scored highest. Thu 19:00 sits in the evening order window two days before the date.

posts.why: From 22 Nov this is the top-left tile, the first thing anyone landing from an ad sees, so it carries the season's hero stone (ruby: 8 of 13 bracelets, 3 of 3 huggies) as a complete set, the basket the economics need (₹5,198 at list; BUY3 takes three pieces to 20% off). It also moves the necklace (70 in stock, unsold). Sunday 12:00 is the top order slot, the day after the first muhurat, with three more that week. The joke rewrites the tailor's board for the guest Naira actually dresses. As the second signboard it closes the long diagonal from P1 and returns the top-left corner to LAC's oxblood. The bill's call-back (graft G5) turns the season into one memory: N° 01 bracelet, N° 07 huggies, N° 09 necklace.
